reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 discusses semi-coherent phase boundaries and work hardening in a different eutectic HEA, with no mention of aging or L12 precipitates. E2 notes L12 precipitates increase strength but also describes precipitate-free channels near interfaces that act as soft sites for dislocation storage, contradicting the claim that precipitates at boundaries reduce pile-ups and stress concentrations.
premises: Low-temperature aging induces nanoscale coherent L12 precipitates at interlamellar boundaries in the eutectic HEA.
These precipitates reduce dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations at boundaries.
Precipitates provide precipitation strengthening, retaining or increasing yield and ultimate tensile strengths.
The intervention improves room-temperature tensile ductility by delaying crack initiation and homogenizing deformation.
